drivers.name: Price increase to $4.56 (+5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two past $4.56 weeks: 2026-09-28 (x0.99), 2026-10-05 (x0.57). Noise-adjusted estimate for price hikes: x0.85. Shrink toward 1.0 due to limited data and high volatility.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A price increase to $4.56 (+5.1%) is the only known driver. Past price spikes at $4.56 show mixed effects: one week (2026-09-28) sold 207 units (x0.99 vs baseline), the next (2026-10-05) sold 119 (x0.57). The noise-adjusted effect of price increases is x0.85 (shrunken from x0.78 due to limited data). No event or promotion is scheduled. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but that ignores price sensitivity. The recent price hike is unusually deep (5.1%) and occurred in a low-sales week (x0.57). We shrink the effect toward 1.0 due to sparse evidence and volatility. No post-promo dip is expected as no promotion occurred recently.

brief:
PRODUCT: Whole Milk 1 gal | category Dairy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-08 (4 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.5 - 290.3 | 10%-90%: 156.3 - 281.1

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
